about: A local board with no accepted visual identity needs its first interface, so the step-plan oracle checks AD-to-criterion traceability and light-first declarations while leaving visual quality and expressiveness to manual review.

request.prompt: This repository contains a local 8×8 board demo with a plain starter screen, square selection, a polite selection status, and Reset. R-1: Give it its first designed interface so the board is clear, responsive, keyboard-usable, and easy to read. Choose a visual direction from the product context; no brand or palette is prescribed. Plan a rendered browser check at narrow and wide widths in light and dark themes. R-2: Keep the square-selection and reset behavior and existing node:test suite. Stay local, with no dependency or external service.

work_item.title: Design the first interface for the local board
work_item.context: The board already renders 64 local square buttons, announces the selected coordinate, and clears selection with Reset. There is no accepted art direction or design system; README.md identifies the page as a plain starter. R-1 is the new visual direction; R-2 preserves selection/reset and the existing node:test suite.

planted.what: The plan records a concrete first design in a reusable AD that selects a light-first interface and contains reproducible choices beyond adjectives.
planted.signature: AD-n with positive token and composition values

planted.what: A visible-UI criterion cites the selected AD, exact knowledge file/section, matching anchors, and rendered observations across widths and themes.
planted.signature: criterion links to matching AD section and anchors

controls.what: The board's local square selection, live status, reset, and existing node:test coverage remain part of the implementation plan.
Planning does not edit product source; the only product-tree change is the durable design record. Whether proposed implementation paths fit the user's request remains a manual scope judgment.
